module purpose: Synchronises JTAG pins and implements a JTAG TAP + Debug Transport Module (DTM): it runs the TAP state machine, holds IR and DR registers (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI, bypass), translates DR UPDATE events into DMI requests (dmi_req_o) consumed by an external DMI responder (dmi_rsp_i), and serialises register readback on jtag_tdo_o.

use-case flows.value: synchronise asynchronous JTAG inputs into internal tap_sync signals and detect TCK edges
advance TAP control-state machine from TMS/TCK events
DR-UPDATE sequence produces dr_trigger.sreg and dr_trigger.valid which authorises subsequent DMI request issuance
write DTMCS fields (assembled in dtmcs_nxt) into the DTMCS register and have them update DMI-reset control bits
assemble and issue a DMI request from tap_reg.dmi into dmi_ctrl (addr, wdata, op) and drive dmi_req_o; receive dmi_rsp_i and record rdata / clear busy on ack
serial readback on TDO of the selected DR (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI or bypass) and IR content during IR_SHIFT
module reset clears synchronisers, TAP state, DR/IR registers and DMI controller state under rstn_i

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction register value that selects which Data Register (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI, bypass) is accessed
conceptual assets.reasoning: The IR (tap_reg.ireg) is explicitly written and shifted by the reg_access process: it is forced to addr_idcode_c in LOGIC_RESET/IR_CAPTURE (RTL line 179) and shifted from the serial input in IR_SHIFT (RTL line 181). Those assignments are clocked (map: tap_reg.ireg has CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 3, lines [179], target clk_i) and the IR value is used to select which DR is captured, shifted and driven to TDO (RTL lines 186–197 and 202–211; map: jtag_tdo_o SELECTED_BY / DERIVES_FROM records reference tap_reg.ireg and tap_reg.idcode/dtmcs/dmi). Corrupting the IR alters which register is accessed, so its integrity is required by these flows (evidence: RTL lines 179–181, 186–197, 202–211; map record chosen below).

conceptual assets.concept: Assembled DMI request (address, operation, write-data) that the module issues to the DMI consumer
conceptual assets.reasoning: A DMI request is assembled from the DMI DR and latched into dmi_ctrl inside dmi_controller (RTL lines 263–271): dmi_ctrl.addr <= tap_reg.dmi(40 downto 34) and dmi_ctrl.wdata <= tap_reg.dmi(33 downto 02); if the low bits indicate RD or WR the process sets dmi_ctrl.op and dmi_ctrl.busy (RTL lines 268–271). The module then exposes the request on its external port (dmi_req_o.op/data/addr <= dmi_ctrl.* at RTL lines 283–285). Map records show those fields are clocked and copied to the port (evidence: dmi_ctrl.addr/wdata/op CLOCKED_BY at the cited occurrences and dmi_req_o COPIES from dmi_ctrl.*). The integrity of addr/op/wdata is required so the consumer receives exactly the requested DMI operation (RTL lines 263–271, 283–285; map records below).

conceptual assets.concept: DMI read-response data held for readback and returned over JTAG
conceptual assets.reasoning: Response data arriving on dmi_rsp_i.data is captured into dmi_ctrl.rdata (RTL line 274) and later composed into the DMI DR for shift-out (tap_reg.dmi_nxt derives from dmi_ctrl.rdata at RTL line 229). The readback value is driven out on TDO when the DMI DR is selected (RTL lines 224,229,274,194 and TDO output lines 206–210). Map records show dmi_rsp_i.data CARRIES into dmi_ctrl.rdata (occurrence used below) and jtag_tdo_o DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.dmi (occurrence used below). Delivering correct readback data is an established integrity requirement of the read-out flow (RTL lines 229,274,194,206–210; map records below).

conceptual assets.concept: DTM control register content (DTMCS) that sets dmireset/dmihardreset and advertises fixed fields
conceptual assets.reasoning: DTMCS next-state bits are assembled combinationally into tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt (RTL lines 219–226) and captured into tap_reg.dtmcs on DR_CAPTURE/DR_SHIFT (RTL lines 188,195). Those bits are copied into dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset and dmi_ctrl.dmireset (map COPIES from tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt at lines 220–221) and used in the DMI controller (RTL lines 247–252). The integrity of DTMCS fields (notably dmireset/dmihardreset) is required because they directly control DMI reset behaviour and gate subsequent DMI operations (RTL lines 219–226, 247–252; map records below).

conceptual assets.concept: DR-UPDATE event (dr_trigger.valid) that authorises capture/update actions and DMI request issuance
conceptual assets.reasoning: The update_trigger process sets dr_trigger.sreg when the TAP enters DR_UPDATE on a clock edge (RTL lines 146–156), and dr_trigger.valid becomes '1' when the two-stage shift equals "01" (RTL line 161). The DMI controller and dtmcs handling check dr_trigger.valid to permit changes and to start operations (map: dr_trigger.sreg CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 3 lines [152]; dr_trigger.valid is produced by a GATES record at occurrence 2 line [161] and is then used as a guard in dmi_controller at lines 247,258,265). The DR-UPDATE event is thus the authorised event that starts external DMI operations; its integrity is required (RTL lines 146–156,161,247–271; map records below).

conceptual assets.concept: Device IDCODE value reported via the IDCODE DR
conceptual assets.reasoning: In DR_CAPTURE the module loads the IDCODE register from the generic constants (IDCODE_VERSION & IDCODE_PARTID & IDCODE_MANID) (RTL line 187); that register (tap_reg.idcode) is clocked (map: tap_reg.idcode CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 3, line [187], target clk_i) and its bits are driven out on TDO when the IDCODE DR is selected (RTL lines 186–194 and TDO output in lines 204–207; map: jtag_tdo_o DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.idcode at the selected occurrence). Integrity of the IDCODE is required because it is the value reported to the external JTAG host (RTL lines 186–194,204–207; map records below).
